text:
Alex: Quick debug run on 8xA100 with KV cache hot-path.
Alex: nvprof + CUPTI traces collected, seeing repeated allreduce tails ~6-8ms per step.
Maria: drop the exact nvprof + cupti commands?
Alex: nvprof command I used:
```
nvprof --profile-from-start off --suppress-error --print-gpu-trace \n  --events gld_load_throughput,gst_load_throughput --log-file nvprof-8gpu.log
```
also created cupti sqlite: cupti-8gpu.sqlite
Sam: upload the traces to the perf bucket?
Alex: perf-bot: uploaded artifacts to gs://redwood-profiles/1955067000/ (nvprof + cupti + nsight)
Maria: quick skim of the nsight timeline: allreduce op appears earlier on some GPUs and lags on others 50-80us jitter but some 3-8ms skew.
Jin: suspect kernel-selection path: we pick microkernels based on seq_len histogram per-shard. different shards can pick different microkernels -> staggered launches.
Tori: repro details?
Alex: synthetic inputs: batch=2, seq lenses [4,128] mixed, tp=2 pp=4, standard shard layout.
Alex: I added a tiny runtime timer in the hot path:
```
ScopedTimer t_allreduce("allreduce", /*accumulate=*/true);
// appends to per-shard ring_times vector
```
Maria: can we compute a comm_comp_ratio = sum(comm_ms)/sum(comp_ms) across GPUs per-step? would highlight imbalance.
Sam: +1, useful for auto-tuning batching heuristics.
Jin: another theory: KV cache warmup causes uneven compute on first tokens -> shifts launch earlier/later by ~3ms and drags ring tail.
Tori: nvprof flame shows repeated small H2D memcpy on lagging shards before they call the allreduce.
Alex: nvprof snippet:
```
== NVIDIA PROFILE ==
GPU 2: memcpy HtoD 2.3ms
GPU 5: memcpy HtoD 1.9ms
GPU 0: allreduce 6.1ms (tail)
```
Maria: possible mitigations:
- prefetch non-critical H2D earlier or overlap with KV cache reads
- force unified microkernel selection across shards for identical config
- align per-device batch multiples so launch times match
Sam: also consider ring schedule resilience: if a shard is busy > X ms, shift ring offsets dynamically to reduce long tails.
Jin: I'll add instrumentation to emit per-kernel launch timestamps across shards so we can quantify skew.
Alex: opened PR with quick instrumentation: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/402
perf-bot: PR 402 linked with artifacts: gs://redwood-profiles/1955067000/
Maria: next run, add light syscall tracing to rule out host-side stalls (pthread mutex or I/O?)
Tori: I'll add gdbsyscall capture for critical path and a lightweight strace on the host threads.
Alex: plan: 1) collect per-kernel launch timestamps 2) compute comm_comp_ratio + launch_skew 3) try forced-unified-kernel-selection and rerun nvprof
Maria: can we schedule a baseline rerun tomorrow 10:00 PT?
Sam: available
Jin: reserving 8-GPU bench and blocking 60m
Tori: tagging infra: @infra-team
infra-bot: @infra-team notified, reservation created: res-9876
Alex: thanks, will post results here after the run.
